# Parity-conditioned consensus: a complete limit and an exact selector obstruction

This note proves a canonical contraction of any compactly supported mixed
probability measure to at most 2^n actual mixed points. It then proves that
ALL resulting points can fail the OC bound, even for an actual convex body
with three simplex fibers. The contraction is therefore not an OC proof.
Its parity weighting differs from globally conditioning two independent
samples to have equal parity: here each parity class is selected with its
original mass, not with the square of that mass.

## 1. The operation and convergence

Let S=C intersect (Z^n times R^d), for compact convex C, and let mu be any
probability measure on S. For each parity r, write p_r=mu(S_r). Define Qmu
by choosing r with probability p_r and then taking (X+X')/2, where X,X'
are independent with law mu restricted to S_r, divided by p_r. Empty
classes contribute zero. Convexity and parity put every output in S.

For every continuous convex ambient function f, Jensen gives

    integral f dQmu <= integral f dmu.                         (1)

The full ambient first moment is unchanged. For E(mu)=integral |x|^2 dmu,
the exact loss is

    E(mu)-E(Qmu) = (1/2) sum_r p_r Var(mu_r/p_r),               (2)

where Var is the trace of the full ambient covariance matrix. In
particular, the loss vanishes precisely when every nonempty parity class
is a point mass.

The map Q is weakly continuous on probabilities on S. Indeed S has only
finitely many integer fibers and every parity class is relatively clopen.
For a bounded continuous test f, the r contribution is

    p_r^(-1) double_integral f((x+x')/2) dmu_r(x)dmu_r(x').

It is continuous when p_r>0. When p_r tends to zero its absolute value is
at most p_r times the supremum of |f|, so it tends to zero as well.

Put mu_t=Q^t mu. Every continuous convex integral converges by (1).
Every ambient polynomial P restricted to compact C is the difference of
two continuous convex functions: choose A large enough that the Hessian
of P+A|x|^2 is positive semidefinite on C, and subtract A|x|^2. Thus all
polynomial integrals converge. Polynomials are uniformly dense in C(S)
by the real Stone-Weierstrass theorem (their restrictions contain
constants and separate points). Consequently every continuous integral
converges. Compactness of probabilities on S supplies a weak limit nu,
unique because continuous functions separate measures. Hence the FULL
sequence mu_t converges weakly to nu.

Weak continuity of Q now gives Qnu=nu, or equivalently (2) and continuity
of E give zero variance within each nonempty parity. Therefore

    nu = sum_(i=1)^k alpha_i delta_(y_i),
    1<=k<=2^n, alpha_i>0, sum alpha_i=1, y_i in S,             (3)

with distinct parity classes for distinct y_i. Its full barycenter equals
that of mu. Neither ordinary centroid rounding nor an affine lattice
change was used.

## 2. A genuine convex body with three simplex fibers

Take n=1,d=4. Let B be the standard 4-simplex with vertices 0,e_1,...,e_4,
volume V, and barycentric coordinate lambda_1=x_1. Set

    beta=199/1000, q=199/100, r=1/100,
    m=q^(-4), a=r^4 m=199^(-4).

Thus q+r=2 and 0<a<1/1000. There exists a 4-simplex L inside B with

    0<=lambda_1<=beta, |L|=mV, (g_L)_1=4 beta/5.              (4)

Here is an explicit construction. Take an apex p in the relative
interior of the face lambda_1=0, and an upper tetrahedron at lambda_1=beta
obtained by a homothety of ratio t about that section's centroid. The full
section has 3-volume (1-beta)^3 times that of the opposite face. The
simplex joining p to the upper tetrahedron has relative 4-volume
beta(1-beta)^3 t^3. Choose

    t=[m/(beta(1-beta)^3)]^(1/3).

This lies in (0,1), as verified by the exact integer comparison in the
accompanying verifier. All five vertices lie in B. One vertex has first
coordinate zero and four have first coordinate beta, proving (4).

Define the two other simplex fibers A=rL and D=qL, where homotheties are
in the ordinary R^4 vector coordinates. Their volumes are aV and V.
Their Minkowski midpoint is exactly L because q+r=2. The convex hull

    C=conv( {-1} times A, {0} times B, {1} times D )           (5)

is an ambient 5-dimensional convex body. Its integer fibers are exactly
A,B,D. At the middle fiber every additional convex combination is a
convex combination of B and (A+D)/2=L subset B. The endpoints are
extreme projection levels, so their fibers remain exact. Thus its
mixed volume is M=(2+a)V.

## 3. The two consensus points

It is convenient to use unnormalized fiber masses, in units of V, whose
sum remains 2+a. Write a_t,b_t,c_t for the masses at -1,0,1. The parity
conditioned operation has the exact recurrence

    a_(t+1)=a_t^2/(a_t+c_t),
    c_(t+1)=c_t^2/(a_t+c_t),
    b_(t+1)=b_t+2a_t c_t/(a_t+c_t),                         (6)

starting from (a,1,1). The difference c_t-a_t=1-a is invariant. Since
a_(t+1)<=a_t/2 whenever c_t>=a_t, a_t tends to zero, c_t tends to 1-a,
and b_t tends to 1+2a.

The continuous conditional means at -1 and 1 remain g_A and g_D: an
endpoint output averages two samples from that same endpoint. Full
moment preservation and Section 1 therefore identify the limiting law:
its two atoms are

    y_+=(1,g_D),
    y_0=(0,h_vec),
    h_vec=(g_B+a g_A+a g_D)/(1+2a)
         =(g_B+2a g_L)/(1+2a),                              (7)

with unnormalized weights 1-a and 1+2a respectively. There are no other
limiting points. In particular, the heavier limiting atom is at y_0.
Both points are in S, as also follows from weak convergence on compact S.

## 4. Both limiting centers fail the exact OC target

At y_+, choose a simplex centroid cap in D of volume gamma_4 V, where
gamma_4=(4/5)^4. Add a sufficiently large coefficient of z to its normal
to exclude the two other compact fibers, while leaving its cut on z=1
unchanged. This is a closed ambient halfspace containing y_+, of mass
gamma_4 V, strictly less than (gamma_4/2)(2+a)V.

For y_0 write its first continuous coordinate as h. By (4) and (7),

    h = 1/5 - (51/625) a/(1+2a).                            (8)

Since a<1/1000, h>beta. Consider the actual closed ambient halfspace

    H={x_1+(1-q) beta z >= h}.                              (9)

At z=-1 its maximum left side is r beta-(1-q)beta=beta;
at z=1 its maximum is q beta+(1-q)beta=beta. Thus BOTH endpoint
fibers are wholly excluded, while y_0 lies on its boundary. On B the
retained cap has volume

    (1-h)^4 V
      = gamma_4 [1+(51/500) a/(1+2a)]^4 V.                 (10)

For 0<a<1/1000, the mean-value theorem bounds the bracket's excess
over one by

    (51/125)(1001/1000)^3 a < a/2.

This last strict comparison is an exact rational inequality. Therefore
(10) is strictly less than gamma_4(1+a/2)V, the OC target. Consequently
neither consensus point satisfies OC.

## 5. Precisely what fails

The iteration has a deterministic, fully proved weak limit supported
on at most 2^n actual mixed points and preserves the ordinary ambient
centroid at every stage. These properties do not give an OC selector.
They also do not give the proposed halfspace domination

    mu(H) >= gamma_d nu({y_i}) whenever y_i in H:

in this example the cap (9) already violates it for the heavier atom,
whose unnormalized limiting weight is 1+2a. The example does NOT refute
OC, convex extraction with adjustable source shapes, or every possible
martingale decomposition. It closes this particular parity-consensus
mechanism, including selecting any of its final atoms.
